name: overflow
desc: What water does when there is simply too much to hold.
prose: Overflow is what water does when there is simply too much. The bath fills past the brim and spills onto the floor; the river swells with rain and climbs its banks; the cup runs over your hand. It is fullness that cannot be held any longer, the moment the vessel gives up and lets go. You cannot catch it - it pours away wherever it likes. Natural and weightless, it is the water saying enough, there is no more room, and brimming over.

lines: Plip. The tap is not quite off,
and now and then, just one
small drop falls down into the sink -
A thin slow thread of running wet,
too small to call a stream;
down the rock it slips and slides -
A salty drop that fills your eye
it falls when you are sad or hurt -
no word you have to speak.
Not proper rain, just tiny drops,
too light for brollies, soft and grey -
